counterfactual_missing_items: positional headache (absent; would be expected in post-dural puncture headache)
biconvex hyperdense extra-axial collection (absent; would favor epidural hematoma)
acute hyperdense crescent without layering (absent; would favor acute subdural hematoma)
decisive_items: 15 mm in width with a 13-mm midline shift
headache was severe, nonpositional, and unrelieved by rest or analgesics
response.rationale: R1 is strongly supported by the chronic subdural imaging pattern: a layered hypodense crescent-shaped extra-axial collection with hyperdense areas and significant midline shift, plus the delayed post-spinal presentation and nonpositional headache. R3 is a reasonable differential due to spinal anesthesia and early headache, but the severe nonpositional headache and CT collection argue against isolated post-dural puncture headache. R4 is weakest because the layered hypodense crescent-shaped morphology contradicts the typical biconvex hyperdense epidural hematoma appearance.

rejected.why: Only the generic 'extra-axial collection' span supports epidural hematoma; the 'layered hypodense crescent-shaped' morphology and chronic progressive timeline are against epidural hematoma.
